title: `reset_physics_interpolation` does not appear to work correctly for `Control` nodes being moved via their anchors
body:
### Tested versions

- First found in: v4.4.1.stable.official [49a5bc7b6]
- Reproduced in: v4.5.beta4.official [2d113cc22]

### System information

Godot v4.5.beta4 - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 3 monitors - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1070 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.7680) - AMD Ryzen 5 1500X Quad-Core Processor (8 threads) - 15.92 GiB memory

### Issue description

When a `Control` is moved via a change of `anchor_left` or `anchor_top`, its visual position is not immediately updated when `reset_physics_interpolation` is called.

For some reason, if you change its position again via the `position` property after changing the anchors (before calling `reset_physics_interpolation`), then it works. This includes something like `position.x += 1.0; position.x -= 1.0`, but not `position.x = position.x`.

MRP footage (physics FPS is 1):

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/caccdcf5-1ef8-4592-9454-29fc8fa625f8

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `Control` node with enabled physics interpolation (in both the project settings and the individual node, since apparently `Control` nodes have this disabled by default?)
2. Create a script that modifies `anchor_left` or `anchor_top` (most obvious if it alternates between two values every frame, at a very low physics FPS) and then calls `reset_physics_interpolation`
3. Observe the position of the `Control` being interpolated when it shouldn't be
   - Optionally, add `position.x += 1.0; position.x -= 1.0` before the call to `reset_physics_interpolation` and notice that the position is now properly being not interpolated

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21565835/issue.zip)
